jobs.title: Design codex — RFC 0048 V1.5 fix-up
jobs.objective: Design RFC 0048 V1.5 fix-up across two tracks. Track A (router + handler internals + transport, codex): (1) fail-closed routing — once a method is registered as PG-backed, every PG handler exception, capability denial, parameter validation failure must return an RPC error and must NOT call striatum.api.invoke / striatum.db.connect / SQLite-backed dispatch (codex F1); (2) audit-chain SERIALIZABLE or row-lock per PG write handler (codex F3); (3) append-only role enforcement: privilege tests that the daemon read-write role cannot UPDATE/DELETE striatumd.events or striatumd.artifacts (codex F4); (4) wire the missing Unix-socket accept loop in src/striatum/daemon.py::run_daemon_foreground so daemon-required CLI verbs actually reach the daemon — this is the gap that forced legacy SQLite mode in dogfood-057. Track B (tests + schema + docs + UX, claude): (1) real byte-equivalence parity tests — wire conftest's Seed dataclass + pg_ctx + sqlite_conn into all 16 handler test files, remove RFC0048_PARITY skipif gating, per-key state diff helper (claude HIGH #1); (2) capability-denial test coverage per handler: missing token, revoked, expired, wrong capability, wrong repository scope, replay (codex F2); (3) dead code cleanup: define or delete complete_inline, ack_inline, recovery.resume --complete, recovery.auto live mode (claude HIGH #2); (4) schema migration 0006 adding striatumd.events.previous_hash, row_hash + striatumd.repo_event_chain_heads head table, re-anchor existing rows from payload_json._event_chain; (5) striatum daemon doctor --explain (or daemon.describe) surfaces which methods are PG-backed vs SQLite-fallback; (6) POSTGRES_TRANSITION.md adds fresh-install role-provisioning runbook (striatumd_rw role with explicit REVOKEs on audit_log/events/artifacts, CREATE on db + schema).

jobs.title: Synth codex — RFC 0048 V1.5 fix-up scope lock
jobs.objective: Reconcile the 3 designs into one concrete fix-up plan with two implementer tracks. Track A (codex, router + transport + handler-internal enforcement): fail-closed routing in DaemonRpcRouter._route, accept loop in run_daemon_foreground, audit-chain SERIALIZABLE / row-lock per handler, append-only privilege checks. Track B (claude, tests + schema + docs + UX): parity rig wired into 16 handler tests with per-key diff, capability-denial test matrix (6 cases per handler), schema migration 0006 (previous_hash + row_hash + repo_event_chain_heads + re-anchor), dead code cleanup, daemon doctor --explain, POSTGRES_TRANSITION.md role-provisioning runbook. Lock exact file paths, function names, test paths, error envelopes. Pick one path. Do NOT enumerate alternatives.

jobs.title: Review design claude ergonomics_dx
jobs.objective: Review synthesis. Mandatory checks: (a) all six codex F1-F4/etc findings + four claude HIGH/MEDIUM/etc findings explicitly addressed with concrete file paths; (b) accept loop design is concrete (exact function name, exact thread/asyncio model, exact bytes flow CLI client → socket → router → handler → response); (c) schema migration 0006 is per-method byte-equivalent for existing rows; (d) parity rig has a real per-key diff helper that prints state_a vs state_b on failure; (e) capability-denial tests enumerate the 6 cases (missing/revoked/expired/wrong-cap/wrong-repo/replay) for every PG write handler. Bounce on any 'TODO' or 'see V1.6' answer that defers a non-negotiable.

jobs.title: Implement Track A — router + transport + handler internals (codex)
jobs.objective: Track A — (1) Wire fail-closed routing in src/striatum/daemon_rpc/server.py::DaemonRpcRouter._route: when method is in the PG handler registry, any handler exception/capability-denial/parameter-validation error returns an RPC error envelope and MUST NOT fall through to CLI_ROUTES. Add a registry method `is_pg_backed(method_name)` and use it as the fork. Add a regression test that monkeypatches a PG handler to raise and asserts no SQLite read/write occurs. (2) Add audit-chain SERIALIZABLE or row-lock per PG write handler: each handler in src/striatum/daemon_pg/handlers/{workflow_loop,recovery_evidence}/ wraps its event-append + state-mutation in a single SERIALIZABLE transaction (or explicit row-lock on a chain-head table). Add a concurrent test that drives overlapping allowed + denied requests across claim, publish-artifact, verdict, complete, recovery; verify single contiguous audit chain, no orphan workflow mutations. (3) Wire the Unix-socket accept loop in src/striatum/daemon.py::run_daemon_foreground — currently binds + listens(1) but never accept()s; add an asyncio or thread-per-connection accept loop that reads RPC envelopes via daemon_rpc.framing, routes through DaemonRpcRouter, returns responses. Tests in tests/daemon_rpc/ exercise CLI client → unix socket → router → handler end-to-end. (4) Append-only role enforcement: SQL changes in src/striatum/daemon_pg/sql/0001_baseline.sql (or new 0007 migration if 0001 is frozen) to grant striatumd_rw the correct privileges. Tests verify striatumd_rw cannot UPDATE/DELETE striatumd.events or striatumd.artifacts. Sub-agents per cluster: fail-closed routing, audit-chain locking, accept loop, role enforcement.

jobs.title: Implement Track B — tests + schema + docs + UX (claude)
jobs.objective: Track B — (1) Wire the parity rig advertised in tests/daemon_pg/handlers/recovery_evidence/conftest.py into all 16 handler test files (9 workflow_loop + 7 recovery_evidence). Add a `parity_seed` fixture that materializes both PG and SQLite state from the same Seed dataclass. Add a per-key state diff helper that prints state_a vs state_b on failure. Remove `@pytest.mark.skipif(not os.environ.get('RFC0048_PARITY'))` so parity tests run by default. (2) Add capability-denial test matrix: for every PG write handler, tests for missing token, revoked, expired, wrong capability, wrong repository scope, replayed request_id. Each test asserts no workflow-table mutation, no audit-row append on the allow path, and a denied audit row with the documented reason. (3) Schema migration 0006 (src/striatum/daemon_pg/sql/0006_event_chain_columns.sql): ALTER TABLE striatumd.events ADD COLUMN previous_hash bytea NOT NULL DEFAULT ..., ADD COLUMN row_hash bytea NOT NULL DEFAULT ...; CREATE TABLE striatumd.repo_event_chain_heads (repository_id text PRIMARY KEY, head_hash bytea NOT NULL, updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL); migration body re-anchors existing rows by reading payload_json._event_chain.previous_hash/row_hash and copying into the new columns. Idempotent re-run via schema_meta version. (4) Dead code cleanup: define or delete `complete_inline`/`ack_inline`/`recovery.resume --complete`/`recovery.auto` live mode. Tests removed/updated. (5) striatum daemon doctor --explain (new flag): adds a per-method table showing which methods are PG-backed vs SQLite-fallback. Equivalent functionality on daemon.describe MCP method (Phase B prep). (6) POSTGRES_TRANSITION.md: new section 'Provision the daemon-required role' showing `CREATE ROLE striatumd_rw WITH LOGIN PASSWORD ...; GRANT CONNECT/USAGE/SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on schema + tables; REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE ON striatumd.{audit_log,events,artifacts}; GRANT CREATE ON DATABASE + SCHEMA`. Cite the daemon doctor refusal that surfaces the missing role. Sub-agents per cluster: parity rig, capability-denial tests, schema migration, dead code cleanup, daemon doctor --explain, doc update.

jobs.title: Build review codex threat_model
jobs.objective: Threat-model review across both tracks: verify F1 fail-closed (test that monkeypatches a PG handler to raise and asserts no SQLite read/write — actual test, not aspirational); verify F2 capability-denial matrix is complete and tests assert denied audit-row content not just no-mutation; verify F3 audit-chain locking actually serializes (concurrent test produces unbroken chain under load); verify F4 role-enforcement REVOKEs are in SQL AND tests assert striatumd_rw cannot UPDATE/DELETE; verify accept loop end-to-end: a real CLI client process can call striatum status against a real daemon and get back a real response (not mocked). Reject if any of those is missing or simulated.

jobs.title: Build review claude ergonomics_dx
jobs.objective: Operator UX review: parity rig produces readable per-key diff on failure (not 'assert False'); daemon doctor --explain output is actionable (operator can run it to find which methods need migration); POSTGRES_TRANSITION.md role-provisioning runbook is copy-pasteable and works on a fresh Ubuntu/macOS Postgres install; capability-denial tests run by default (no env-gating); dead code paths actually removed (no orphaned imports); v1.49.0 → v1.50.0 path is clean (no SQL migration that requires manual intervention beyond daemon doctor --apply-migrations).

jobs.title: Build review gemini adversarial
jobs.objective: Adversarial: a PG handler raises mid-transaction and the chain breaks (partial event row + missing workflow row); replay attack against fail-closed routing (a duplicate request_id is somehow accepted by the new accept-loop path); accept loop accepts an envelope from a non-authorized client; audit-chain SERIALIZABLE deadlocks under concurrent load and the code retries silently corrupting the chain; schema migration 0006 leaves orphan rows for repositories whose payload_json._event_chain is malformed; capability-denial test that passes for the wrong reason (e.g., a handler that returns the same response on missing-token AND invalid-token); a non-PG-backed CLI method that the new accept loop routes incorrectly.
